newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Security tightened around Austria's Vranitzky.
newsitem.headline: Security tightened around Austria's Vranitzky.

text.p: Security was stepped up around Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky on Tuesday after he was named as one of the targets of a guerrilla threat to blow up prominent people in Austria and abroad.

Vranitzky was flanked by two bodyguards -- a rare sight in Austria's low-key security system -- when he attended an exhibition with Lea Rabin, the widow of assassinated Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

A group calling itself the Bajuvarian Liberation Army (BLA) had written to current affairs magazine Profil warning that it planned to target eight well-known figures in a renewed offensive, an interior ministry spokesman said. Vranitzky did not comment on the bomb threats.

Government sources have indicated that the BLA may consist of a group of middle-aged fanatics who are believed to be obsessed with reuniting German-speaking peoples in Bavaria, the Alps and the Danube River -- a distinct region which existed between the sixth and 12th centuries.
The alert came amid of campaigning for elections to the European Parliament and a Vienna state poll on October 13.

Officials said the eight targets lived in Austria and abroad but they declined to identify them or name the countries involved. But Austrian radio quoted the interior ministry as saying the Social Democrat chancellor, one of Europe's longest-serving heads of government, was among them.

Police chiefs confirmed the note was authentic, because it bore the same hallmarks as messages attached by the group to letter bombs that have either exploded or been intercepted by police since the campaign began in December 1993.

According to a copy of the 20-page note obtained by Austrian newsagency APA, the BLA branded Vranitzky a "Slavonic chief and devourer of Germans", who "acted as Father Christmas for (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat".

This last quote lies in apparent contradiction to the fact that Vranitzky in 1991 broke new ground by acknowledging Austria shared responsibility for the crimes committed by Nazi Germany. Two years later he became the first chancellor to visit Israel.

The BLA has claimed responsibility for more than 20 letter bombs directed against foreigners and figures linked to immigrant or refugee issues since 1993. Eleven people have been injured in the attacks.

In possibly connected incidents, four gypsy men died last year when a booby-trapped bomb exploded as they tried to remove a racist sign. And a police officer was maimed in 1994 when a pipe bomb went off outside a Slovenian language school.

Despite questioning around 50,000 people and poring over 400,000 pages of related reports, police remain baffled by the bombings, drawing widespread public criticism of the state's security apparatus.
The only arrests have been of two young neo-Nazis who were acquitted in December 1995. No one has been charged with the murders of the four gypsies.
